theorems.claim: Retaining an additional non-destructive reference channel weakly contracts compatible-world and identified sets relative to the primary observation alone.
assumptions: the reference is retained as an additional observation rather than replacing the primary observation
reference acquisition does not silently redefine the primary observation process
theorems.empirical_boundary: Whether a physical reference produces strict contraction for a scientifically relevant estimand is empirical.

theorems.claim: A deterministic coarsening of a rich evidence record weakly expands compatible-world and identified sets.
assumptions: coarsening is a deterministic function of the rich record
theorems.empirical_boundary: The practical size of the resulting uncertainty expansion depends on the application and record distribution.

theorems.claim: In Y=S+N with unrestricted S and N, primary-only target/nuisance decomposition is not identifiable.
assumptions: S and N are unrestricted over a common additive vector space
theorems.proof_type: constructive observational equivalence via S+Delta and N-Delta
theorems.empirical_boundary: Domain restrictions can restore partial or point identification and must be justified separately.

theorems.claim: For an orthogonal projector P, target-to-nuisance energy ratio improves exactly when the nuisance capture fraction a_N exceeds target capture fraction a_S.
assumptions: P is an orthogonal projector
target and nuisance vectors are nonzero
performance quantity is the defined energy ratio
theorems.empirical_boundary: Values of a_N and a_S for a physical system are empirical.

theorems.claim: Any nonzero reference-only projector can completely erase at least one target in an unrestricted target class.
assumptions: projector is nonzero
target class contains nonzero vectors in projector range
theorems.empirical_boundary: A restricted target class may avoid the counterexample but the restriction requires domain justification.

theorems.claim: The decomposition pair (PY,(I-P)Y) is exactly invertible because the two components sum to Y.
assumptions: both decomposition channels are retained without lossy alteration
theorems.empirical_boundary: Numerical quantization, lossy compression or omitted provenance can break practical reversibility.

theorems.claim: For a fixed decision problem and loss, richer retained observation cannot worsen minimum achievable decision risk; deterministic coarsening cannot improve it.
assumptions: decision maker may use any rule measurable in the retained observation
decision problem and loss are fixed
theorems.empirical_boundary: A restricted or misspecified implemented learner may fail to achieve the information-theoretic optimum.

theorems.claim: If true nuisance lies in a reference-derived nuisance-compatible set, true target signal lies in the translated target-compatible set; calibrated nuisance-set coverage transfers to target-set coverage in the exact additive model.
assumptions: Y=S+N
primary Y is treated as exactly observed for the basic result
theorems.empirical_boundary: Calibration of the physical nuisance-compatible set is empirical.

theorems.claim: Under a norm metric in the additive model, target-compatible set diameter equals nuisance-compatible set diameter.
assumptions: Y=S+N
diameter uses a translation/reflection-invariant norm metric
theorems.empirical_boundary: How narrow the nuisance set can be made by a physical reference is empirical.

theorems.claim: For arbitrary Y=F(S,M), contraction of the compatible measurement-state set M(R) implies contraction of the compatible target set defined by existential inversion through F.
assumptions: the forward relation F and compatible measurement-state set are well-defined
theorems.empirical_boundary: Scientific validity of F and reference-induced restrictions on M require domain evidence.

theorems.claim: Under exact compatible-set inference, reference refinement cannot reduce point-identification coverage and semantic coarsening cannot increase it.
assumptions: resolvability means the estimand is singleton over the complete compatible-world fiber
theorems.proof_type: pointwise monotonicity of singleton identified sets under set inclusion
theorems.empirical_boundary: Approximate observers may fail to represent the true compatible sets and can violate the ideal behavior.

theorems.claim: For arbitrary Y=F(S,M), any valid reference-derived compatible set that covers the true measurement state also induces a target-compatible set covering the true target; probabilistic measurement-state coverage transfers to target-state coverage.
assumptions: the true world satisfies Y=F(S,M)
the target-compatible set is defined by existential inversion over the reference-derived measurement-state set
theorems.empirical_boundary: Constructing a calibrated physical measurement-state set with the declared coverage is empirical; unsupported contraction can destroy coverage.

overall_empirical_boundary: calibration and validity of physical measurement-state compatible sets
named causal attribution without additional structural or interventional assumptions
